title: A member archived at the desk stays on the gym leaderboard and keeps getting the gym's app messages
what: When the owner archives a member who left, the gym list, check-in, plan card and phone sign-in all treat them as gone. But the member app keeps them in the gym: their name still ranks in the top 10 that other members see, they keep reading every gym-wide message (gym closed, offers), their gym-mate profile stays open, and their workouts still feed the busy-machine tips. Only the member pressing Leave in their own app takes them out.
expected: Archiving a member takes them off the leaderboard, gym-mate list and busy-machine counts, and stops new gym messages reaching them, the same as when they leave from the app; restoring brings them back.
how_often: every archived member who still has the app
fix_line: Treat an archived list member as left in the member app reads (leaderboard, messages, gym mates, busy counts)

title: The AI Assistant gives a lower profit for the month than the Expenses page, because it leaves out shop sales
what: The Expenses page counts shop orders handed over this month as money in, next to fees. When the owner asks the AI Assistant for this month's profit, it adds up fees only, while still taking off the stock bought for the shop. A gym that sells supplements sees a smaller profit, or a loss, in the assistant than on the Expenses page for the same month.
expected: The assistant's profit for a month matches the Expenses page: fees plus shop money in, minus expenses.
who: owners who sell in the shop
how_often: every profit question in a month with shop sales
fix_line: Pass the shop orders into the assistant's month profit, as the Expenses page does
